FACULTY SENATE OFFICE FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION NOVEMBER 14, 2024 Curri culum & Standards Committee Report 2024-2025-03B At the October 31, 2024 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate PROGRAM MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES: BS Environmental and Natural Resource Economics, Effective Winter 2025 Appendix A College of Business added TMD to their programs and any course code offered by COB qualifies as concentration credits for our ENRE degree tracks (Green Markets and Sustainability option and Green Business double major).
We propose to add the TMD code to our existing list of accepted COB courses (ACC, BAI, FIN, MGT, MKT, SCA, INE).
BS Medical Laboratory Science, Effective Spring 2025 Appendix B The proposed change involves the addition of six courses that would qualify as "Professional Electives" towards the MLS degree.

Namely, the added courses are: BIO 331 (Parasitology), CMB 312 (Introductory Biochemistry Laboratory), CMB 332 (Medical and Public Health Microbiology Laboratory), CMB 353 (Genetics Laboratory), CMB 491 (Research in Cell and Molecular Biology), and PHP 405 (Fundamentals of Epidemiology).
The addition of these courses accomplishes two goals.
First and foremost, they provide addition al opportunities for students to cultivate lab skills in areas that are relevant to MLS (BIO 331, CMB 312, CMB 332, CMB 353 and CMB 491) as well as explore MLS-related fields (BIO 331, PHP 405) that represent potential career pathways with a MLS degree.
Second, these additional courses provide more flexibility for students to successfully complete the six credit "Professional Elective" requirement of the MLS major in a timely manner.
This is due to the fact that many of the previously approved professional electives have prerequisite course requirements and limited scheduling options (i.e. offered only during fall or spring semester), which can make it challenging for students to complete this degree requirement.

NEW CERTIFICATES, MINORS, or SPECIALIZATIONS COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: Minor - Biochemical Engineering, Effective Spring 2025 Appendix H The Biochemical Engineering minor introduces students to the fundamental chemistry and physics underlying biological processes.
Students will apply engineering principles in a biological context to control the interactions between and behavior of organic molecules, proteins, and other biomacromolecules.
With this minor, students will be prepared for industrial and research positions in the biotechnology and biomedical fields.
The Biochemical Engineering minor is comprised of a minimum of 18 credit hours, at least half of which must be earned at URI.
The required courses include two fundamental science courses (6 credits), two biochemical engineering fundamentals courses (6 credits), and two or more supporting courses (6 credits).
Up to 6 credits can double count towards a major (e.g., core courses).
Students declaring this major must earn a minimum grade point average of 2.00 in courses counted towards the minor.

Students will need to complete the Biochemical Engineering minor form and have it signed by the minor coordinator, department chair, and ap propriate dean.
Students are responsible for meeting the prerequisite requirements for individual courses, as applicable.
